title: Think Differently About Emergencies Act
official_summary:
Think Differently About Emergencies Act

This act requires the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) and the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to report to Congress regarding assistance and resources provided by FEMA to persons with intellectual and developmental disabilities and the families of such individuals who are impacted by major disasters.

Specifically, FEMA must report within 120 days of this act's enactment, describing the assistance and resources that FEMA provides to such individuals and families through states, localities, nonprofit organizations, and individuals.

Further, FEMA and GAO must each (1) review such assistance and resources, (2) identify potential legal impediments to providing such assistance and resources, and (3) provide recommendations to Congress.

summary.headline: Requires FEMA and the GAO to report to Congress on disaster help for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities and their families.
summary.what_it_does: FEMA must send Congress a report within 120 days describing the help and resources it gives, through states, local governments, nonprofits, and individuals, to people with intellectual and developmental disabilities and their families after major disasters. FEMA and the Government Accountability Office (GAO) must each review this help, point out any legal barriers to providing it, and make recommendations to Congress. The law calls for reports and reviews; it does not itself change benefits or create new programs.

who_it_affects.group: People with intellectual and developmental disabilities and their families
who_it_affects.how: The disaster help they receive from FEMA will be reviewed, and Congress will get recommendations that could shape future aid.
FEMA must report to Congress within 120 days and also review its assistance, identify legal barriers, and make recommendations.
GAO must do its own review of FEMA's assistance, identify legal barriers, and make recommendations to Congress.

who_it_affects.group: State and local governments and nonprofit organizations
who_it_affects.how: Their role in passing FEMA help to these individuals and families will be described and reviewed in the reports.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted November 25, 2024; FEMA's first report is due within 120 days (by about March 25, 2025).
